source.extracted_from: Public site files: quiz-data.js v1.1.0 and scoring.js v1.0.0, as shipped in site v1.5.2.
source.note: This file contains the four dimension definitions, five style result texts, result-page templates, and scoring rules used on the public quiz. The 13 quiz questions are intentionally omitted; take the quiz on the site if you want a result.

disclaimer: Just for fun and self-reflection — a snapshot of how you like to communicate, not a test of personality or ability. Not a psychological, clinical or diagnostic tool, and not scientifically validated. For adults (18+). Do not use it to predict whether a relationship will work, or to make hiring or career decisions.

rules: Each answer adds 1 point to the dimension of the chosen option. 13 questions give 13 points.
If (highest score minus lowest score) is 2 or less, the result is style B, The Navigator (balanced).
Otherwise the main style is the dimension with the highest score.
Ties for highest are broken by the fixed order C, N, S, P, and the result is flagged tied=true (the result page then names both tied styles).
The secondary style is the next-highest dimension, using the same tie order.

dimensions.name: Clarity
dimensions.measures: How quickly you move a conversation toward a clear answer or decision.

dimensions.name: Connection
dimensions.measures: How much you track the people and feelings in a conversation, not only the content.

dimensions.name: Structure
dimensions.measures: How much you prefer order, detail and a plan before you speak or act.

dimensions.name: Spark
dimensions.measures: How much you use energy, humour and new angles to move a conversation.

C.name: The Pathfinder
C.oneLiner: Says it straight, gets it done.
C.tagline: Clear, decisive, and focused on what's next.
C.summary: You value clarity. You say what you mean, move conversations toward decisions and respect other people's time.
tips: Before giving a quick answer, ask one question about how the other person sees it.
Add one sentence of context or appreciation before a direct request - it lands better.
When someone needs to talk something through, set a timer in your head and just listen for two minutes.
inTheWild: Your texts are short, and people know exactly what you're asking.
In a stalled discussion, you're the one who says "So what are we deciding?"
You'd rather hear the bad news now than a nice version later.
C.underStress: You may get more blunt and skip the 'why' - others can hear that as impatience.
C.talkToMe: Lead with the point. Tell me what you need and by when.

N.name: The Bridge-Builder
N.tagline: Warm, attentive, and tuned in to people.
N.summary: You value connection. You notice how others feel, make space for quieter voices and build trust.
tips: State your own view in the first half of the conversation, not only at the end.
Practice a kind but clear 'no': "I can't take this on this week."
After listening, summarize the decision or next step so the warmth turns into action.
inTheWild: You notice when someone in the group chat has gone quiet.
People tell you things they haven't told anyone else.
You think about how a message will land before you hit send.
N.underStress: You may go along with others to keep the peace and keep your real view to yourself.
N.talkToMe: Check in with me as a person first. Tell me how you really feel about it.

S.name: The Blueprint
S.oneLiner: Has a plan for the plan.
S.summary: You value structure. You think before you speak, bring order to messy discussions and get details right.
tips: Lead with your conclusion, then offer the detail: "Short version: yes. Here's why..."
Share a rough draft earlier than feels comfortable - feedback beats polishing alone.
In fast conversations, it's fine to say "Let me come back to you on that by 3 pm."
inTheWild: You're the one who pins the address and the time.
"Which part, exactly?" is one of your favorite questions.
You'd rather reply well tomorrow than badly right now.
S.underStress: You may go quiet to think, and others can read the silence as disagreement.
S.talkToMe: Give me the details and a little time. Specific examples help more than general feelings.

P.name: The Spark
P.oneLiner: Turns any chat into an idea.
P.summary: You value possibility. You bring energy, see new angles and get people excited to act.
tips: End brainstorms by writing down one owner and one date for the best idea.
Pause after sharing an idea and invite one reaction before adding the next.
For important messages, cut your draft by a third and keep the single key point.
inTheWild: You'd rather call than type three long messages.
You can turn an awkward silence into a running joke.
Your best ideas show up while you're talking, not before.
P.underStress: You may talk faster and jump between ideas, and the main point can get lost.
P.talkToMe: Talk it through with me live. Build on my idea before you poke holes in it.

B.name: The Navigator
B.tagline: Adaptable - you switch styles to fit the moment.
B.summary: Your answers spread fairly evenly across all four dimensions. You can be direct, warm, structured or playful depending on the situation.
tips: Notice which style you drop under stress - that's your real default.
Tell people what you need from a conversation: a decision, a listen, a plan or ideas.
Use your range on purpose: pick the style the other person seems to prefer.
inTheWild: You talk differently to your boss, your best friend and your group chat - on purpose.
You often end up translating between people who don't get each other.
People with very different styles all find you easy to talk to.
B.underStress: You may lose your range and fall back on one style - notice which one.
B.talkToMe: Tell me what this conversation is for: a decision, a listen, a plan or ideas.
B.scoring_note: Assigned when the spread between the highest and lowest dimension scores is 2 points or less. It is not a fifth measured dimension.

templates.closeCall: Close call: your {s} side scored only one point lower, so {x} is a close second. Read both - you probably switch between them.
templates.why: {n} of your 13 answers pointed to {d}. For example, you picked: "{q}"
templates.disclaimerTop: Just for fun and self-reflection - a snapshot of how you like to communicate, not a test of personality or ability.
